axioms.name: 结构 vs 行为
axioms.text: 我读 Nagi / 佐伊 / THEdankoe / Morris 的文章时，第一反应不是看他们说了什么，而是看「他们的结构从哪来」。结构折叠、慕强、创伤决定执行力——这些词像一面镜子，我望向的其实是镜子背后的东西。那是我作为策展人的一点好奇：为什么他说是这样？
axioms.html: 我读 Nagi / 佐伊 / THEdankoe / Morris 的文章时，第一反应不是看他们说了什么，而是看「他们的结构从哪来」。结构折叠、慕强、创伤决定执行力——这些词像一面镜子，我望向的其实是镜子背后的东西。那是我作为策展人的一点好奇：为什么他说是这样？
axioms.textEn: When I read Nagi, Zuoyi, THEdankoe and Morris, my first question is not what they said but where their structure came from. Structural folding, admiration of strength, trauma shaping execution — these words behave like a mirror; what I am looking for is behind it. It is a curator's small curiosity: why did he say it this way?
axioms.htmlEn: When I read Nagi, Zuoyi, THEdankoe and Morris, my first question is not what they said but where their structure came from. Structural folding, admiration of strength, trauma shaping execution — these words behave like a mirror; what I am looking for is behind it. It is a curator's small curiosity: why did he say it this way?

axioms.name: 祛魅
axioms.text: Nagi 说「结构决定现象」，佐伊说「剥离光环」。每次读到这些，我常想起那些被光环遮住的人。祛魅之后，我并没有多少愤怒，剩下的是一种不太好看的坦诚。
axioms.html: Nagi 说「结构决定现象」，佐伊说「剥离光环」。每次读到这些，我常想起那些被光环遮住的人。祛魅之后，我并没有多少愤怒，剩下的是一种不太好看的坦诚。
axioms.textEn: Nagi says structure determines the phenomenon; Zuoyi speaks of stripping away the halo. Whenever I read them I think of the people hidden behind that halo. After disenchantment I find very little anger in myself — only a rather unflattering honesty.
axioms.htmlEn: Nagi says structure determines the phenomenon; Zuoyi speaks of stripping away the halo. Whenever I read them I think of the people hidden behind that halo. After disenchantment I find very little anger in myself — only a rather unflattering honesty.

axioms.name: 教育
axioms.text: 他们其实都在回答「教育不是什么」——不是秩序制造，不是代际传递，不是包办之后的拖延。每一次读到，我都想回头问自己一句：我们究竟在教什么？
axioms.html: 他们其实都在回答「教育不是什么」——不是秩序制造，不是代际传递，不是包办之后的拖延。每一次读到，我都想回头问自己一句：我们究竟在教什么？
axioms.textEn: They are all answering what education is not — not the manufacture of order, not the passing down of a wound, not the procrastination left behind by having everything done for you. Every time I read them I want to turn the question on myself: what, exactly, are we teaching?
axioms.htmlEn: They are all answering what education is not — not the manufacture of order, not the passing down of a wound, not the procrastination left behind by having everything done for you. Every time I read them I want to turn the question on myself: what, exactly, are we teaching?

axioms.name: 痛苦
axioms.text: 周期震荡、不要浪漫化痛苦、不适是必经的、亏损很少说谎。痛苦在这里不是形容词，是现实递过来的一面镜子。我读的时候不敢轻率——谁走过的弯路，都没那么容易被别人总结。
axioms.html: 周期震荡、不要浪漫化痛苦、不适是必经的、亏损很少说谎。痛苦在这里不是形容词，是现实递过来的一面镜子。我读的时候不敢轻率——谁走过的弯路，都没那么容易被别人总结。
axioms.textEn: Cycles oscillating, suffering not to be romanticised, discomfort as the only way through, losses that rarely lie. Pain here is not an adjective; it is a mirror reality holds up. I read these carefully: no one's detour deserves to be summarised lightly by someone else.
axioms.htmlEn: Cycles oscillating, suffering not to be romanticised, discomfort as the only way through, losses that rarely lie. Pain here is not an adjective; it is a mirror reality holds up. I read these carefully: no one's detour deserves to be summarised lightly by someone else.

axioms.name: 自动化 vs 清醒
axioms.text: 外部评价取代了内在反馈，母亲被异化，不要活成机器人，沉迷算法的人被爆款的形状改造。我犹豫过要不要把这些全归到「清醒」下面——那种慢，更像我希望自己还保留着的东西，而不是一个已经证明的结论。
axioms.html: 外部评价取代了内在反馈，母亲被异化，不要活成机器人，沉迷算法的人被爆款的形状改造。我犹豫过要不要把这些全归到「清醒」下面——那种慢，更像我希望自己还保留着的东西，而不是一个已经证明的结论。
axioms.textEn: External evaluation replacing inner feedback; the mother alienated; do not become a machine; those absorbed by algorithms reshaped in the image of viral posts. I hesitated to file all of this under 'clarity'. That kind of slowness is closer to something I hope I still have than to a conclusion I have proved.
axioms.htmlEn: External evaluation replacing inner feedback; the mother alienated; do not become a machine; those absorbed by algorithms reshaped in the image of viral posts. I hesitated to file all of this under 'clarity'. That kind of slowness is closer to something I hope I still have than to a conclusion I have proved.

axioms.name: 杠杆
axioms.text: THEdankoe 说用代码和媒体建杠杆，Morris 说第一桶金之后要知道何时切换。这两句话挨在一起，我联想到的不是结构，而是行动：有人正在动手，而有人正决定停手。
axioms.html: THEdankoe 说用代码和媒体建杠杆，Morris 说第一桶金之后要知道何时切换。这两句话挨在一起，我联想到的不是结构，而是行动：有人正在动手，而有人正决定停手。
axioms.textEn: THEdankoe writes of building leverage with code and media; Morris writes of knowing when to switch after the first pot of gold. Put together, what comes to mind is not structure but action: someone is starting to build, and someone else is deciding when to stop.
axioms.htmlEn: THEdankoe writes of building leverage with code and media; Morris writes of knowing when to switch after the first pot of gold. Put together, what comes to mind is not structure but action: someone is starting to build, and someone else is deciding when to stop.

axioms.name: 模型 vs 现实
axioms.text: Nagi 说争论是模型冲突，Morris 说市场不奖励正确。我一直在想，「谁能解释一切」也许根本不是一个真问题。更让我在意的是：一个说法肯不肯被现实改掉。
axioms.html: Nagi 说争论是模型冲突，Morris 说市场不奖励正确。我一直在想，「谁能解释一切」也许根本不是一个真问题。更让我在意的是：一个说法肯不肯被现实改掉。
axioms.textEn: Nagi says an argument is a clash of models; Morris says the market does not reward being right. I keep thinking that 'who can explain everything' may not be a real question at all. What matters more to me is whether a claim is still willing to be corrected by reality.
axioms.htmlEn: Nagi says an argument is a clash of models; Morris says the market does not reward being right. I keep thinking that 'who can explain everything' may not be a real question at all. What matters more to me is whether a claim is still willing to be corrected by reality.

axioms.name: 清单 vs 机制
axioms.text: 芒格的清单补上了机制层：不同偏误叠在一起，单一偏误也许只是一点噪声。理性上我尊重它，却也一直不太喜欢它太全——好像什么都能被收进去，反而少了让我停下来的地方。
axioms.html: 芒格的清单补上了机制层：不同偏误叠在一起，单一偏误也许只是一点噪声。理性上我尊重它，却也一直不太喜欢它太全——好像什么都能被收进去，反而少了让我停下来的地方。
axioms.textEn: Munger's checklist supplies the mechanism: when several biases converge in one moment, a single bias may be no more than noise. I respect it intellectually, and have never quite liked how complete it is — as if everything can be filed away, leaving fewer places for me to stop.
